newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian reading-pen maker IRIS mulls listing.
newsitem.headline: Belgian reading-pen maker IRIS mulls listing.

text.p: Belgian Image Recognition Integrated Systems SA (IRIS), maker of an optical character recognition (OCR) pen, said on Wednesday it was mulling a bourse listing by 1999.
"We hope to be ready for a stock market listing within two years," IRIS director Pierre De Muelenaere told a news conference.
KB-Securities director Michel Vanderkeilen said the new EASDAQ bourse would be the most likely market for the IPO.
IRIS on Wednesday announced a 62.5 million franc ($1.9 million) capital increase, which will be placed with institutional investors by KB-Securities and Credit General.
Both underwriters plan to keep between eight and ten percent of IRIS stock, while the owners -- De Muelenaere and Pierre Rion -- will keep at least 50 percent.
De Muelenaere and Rion acquired IRIS in a 1992 management buy out from Belgian holding company Electrorail.
The proceeds of the capital issue will be used to promote the different applications of the company's IRISPen in translation, banking and other areas.
The IRISPen, which costs less than $300 (10,000 Belgian francs), is a pen-sized scanner which allows text to be entered into Windows applications line by line.
"This is the smallest scanner in the world. It is a unique product, we have no competition," De Muelenaere said.

Later this month, IRIS plans to release the IRISPen Translator, which will translate English text into Japanese, French and German. Other versions are also planned. Combined with a sound card, the translator also reads out text aloud.

De Muelenaere said the IRISPen's translations would not be perfect enough to be used in copy for publication, but that it would provide a rough base for final translation. It will also allow a travelling Japanese executive to scan an English newspaper article and get a Japanese text in Kanji script.
IRIS is also the world's second-biggest -- after U.S. firm Caere Corp -- producer of software for flatbed scanners, De Muelenaere said.
"Our aim is to conquer the OCR market, which is about to explode," Rion said, adding that scanners were currently among the best-selling office automation applications.
IRIS, founded in 1987, had a 1996 net profit of 12 million francs on turnover of 250 million francs. It expects a 1997 profit of 25 to 30 million francs on turnover of 330 million francs.
It employed 55 people at the end of 1996. The company's current worth is valued at 400 to 500 million francs. ($ = 32.83 Belgian Francs)
